column4: cleat#2654/cleat#2666: MSSQL-only by nature, not by omission -- event_data is JSONB on Postgres and JSON on MySQL, and both dialects validate JSON syntax at INSERT and refuse this test's malformed literal before awaitEvent ever runs (measured: Postgres returns "pq: invalid input syntax for type json (22P02)" on the seeding insert itself). MSSQL's event_data is NVARCHAR(MAX), a plain text column with no such check, which is exactly why the original corruption this test reproduces (cleat#2645's CI failure) was only ever observed on that dialect. Checks os.Getenv via testutil.TestDB(t, testutil.DialectMSSQL) directly (no subtests), so it skips once, at the top level, in ci.yml's test-go/plugins job (PostgreSQL only via CLEAT_TEST_DB) and runs wherever CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL is set. Renamed from TestAwaitEventMarshalFailureLeavesEventUnconsumed when cleat#2666 changed the test's own assertion (dead-letter instead of leaving the row unconsumed); the skip mechanism and reason are unchanged, only the name. Measured: go test ./plugins/eventtriggers/... -run TestAwaitEventMarshalFailureDeadLettersTheEventInstead -count=1 -json | grep '"Action":"skip"' with CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL unset reports exactly this one skip.

cleat#2666: same mechanism and reason as the line above -- MSSQL-only, checks os.Getenv via testutil.TestDB(t, testutil.DialectMSSQL) directly, no subtests, skips once at the top level. New test added alongside the rename above; proves the issue's actual acceptance criterion (a valid event behind a poison one is still delivered). Measured: go test ./plugins/eventtriggers/... -run TestAwaitEventSkipsAPoisonRowAndDeliversTheNextRealEventInTheSameCall -count=1 -json | grep '"Action":"skip"' with CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL unset reports exactly this one skip.

cleat#2666: same mechanism and reason as the two lines above, in plugins/webhookingest rather than plugins/eventtriggers -- MSSQL-only, checks os.Getenv via testutil.TestDB(t, testutil.DialectMSSQL) directly, no subtests, skips once at the top level. Proves webhookingest's own PoisonEvent wrap specifically, not the shared claim.go mechanism the other two lines' tests already cover. Measured: go test ./plugins/webhookingest/... -run TestAwaitWebhookPoisonPayloadDeadLettersTheEventInstead -count=1 -json | grep '"Action":"skip"' with CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL unset reports exactly this one skip.
